name: Kluft
prior: Stick-slip creak synthesis is an academic/toolkit tradition, not a product: van den Doel JASS 'creaking' demo (UBC; mass on spring with static friction proportional to normal force, 'higher normal force causes longer sticking, therefore a lower creaking frequency' = exactly Kluft's load-to-rate axis; VS: cs.ubc.ca/~kvdoel/jass/creaking); Thoret/Aramaki/Kronland-Martinet DAFx 2013 'Controlling a non linear friction model for evocative sound synthesis' (one model -> creaky door, singing glass, squeaking wet plate; source/resonance, linear filtering; VS: dafx.de paper archive, hal-00866216); SuperCollider MCLDUGens Friction UGen (mass on a belt sticks/slips, author notes 'a musical effect rather than a faithful creak'; VS: plugin.sccode.org/MCLDUGens/Help/Friction.html); Sound Design Toolkit elasto-plastic friction (Max/Pd, GPLv3, pre-sliding, break-away, Stribeck velocity, 'rubbing, braking and squeaky doors'; VS: sdt.lim.di.unimi.it docs, github.com/SkAT-VG/SDT, cycling74.com/packages/sound-design-toolkit); Udine mass-spring-damper bank rubbed with a nonlinear static friction model (VS: air.uniud.it/handle/11390/1232166); friction-drum elasto-plastic model DAFx20in21 paper 32 (VS: vbn.aau.dk). Hardware: Konstantine Croak (Eurorack prototype, 'extended acoustic techniques', users hear 'an elephant stuck on a creaking door', mechanism undocumented; VS: modulargrid.net/e/konstantine-croak), STG .VCO relaxation core (plain relaxation oscillator; VS: sonicstate.com 2019). Hopkin 'Adventures in Friction': predictable pitch needs one side with a strong resonance (VS: barthopkin.com) - i.e. real creak pitch is resonator-set, Kluft's rate-set pitch is a design choice, not physics. Myzel: no friction engine; sisters Harz/Zapfen (from the idea text) use friction as exciter only. Not found anywhere: a touch instrument where one finger axis walks a stick-slip oscillator from 1-2 creaks/s to a locked note. Bowed-string/BandedWG friction (STK, Faust pm.lib) is 'common' but is tone-only (R: synthesis.md 2.10-2.11).
costNotes: Worklet is required (per-sample stick/slip state, slip impulses shorter than 128 frames). Per voice: node 0.06 + 3 k-rate params 0.09 (R: webaudio.md section 4) + per-sample DSP: spring/friction integrator ~5 ns, click resonator + 4 modes = 5 resonators ~25 ns, tanh table ~10 ns, random walk ~3 ns -> ~45 ns/sample = 0.22 % core = 0.37 units; total ~0.5 (idea says 0.45; fine). L3 (two surfaces, 8 modes, cross-coupling): ~0.95. Phone x1.0-1.5 (A). Native fallback as specified (impulse PeriodicWave + noise FM jitter -> 4 BQ): osc + driftBuf gain + 4 BQ + 5 gains ~ 11 nodes = 0.35 + BQ premium ~ 0.55; but it cannot do the rhythm regime: an OscillatorNode at 1.7-20 Hz with an impulse PeriodicWave gives a soft band-limited blip (Blink table 4096 pts, partials capped; R: webaudio.md section 7) and no slip-to-slip variance, so the fallback is a buzz-only stand-in - better to hide the engine without worklet than ship it. Implementation hazard: the block/spring/friction constants must be normalised to the target period (stiffness ~ f^2, slip duration << 1/f), otherwise at 400+ Hz the block never re-sticks (continuous sliding = hiss/silence) and at 2 Hz the slip is too slow to click; the k-rate 'freq' param should scale the whole model, not only the drive. Hysteresis on the rhythm/tone edge belongs in the processor, not in the main thread (Hoehe arrives smoothed at 40 ms).
soundHeld: Three regimes under one finger: y < ~0.5 = irregular creaks at 1.5-30/s (each slip = click into a tuned 4-mode body: this is the strong, genuinely new part - a rhythm the body pitches to the note, with +-30 % random walk so it never loops); 0.5-0.75 = 20-80 Hz 'motorboat' zone, rough and unstable, the most creak-like region but also where pitch identity is absent; y > ~0.75 = a jittered impulse train at f through 5 resonators = a nasal, buzzy inharmonic tone (ratios 1:2.756:5.404:8.933 'stone' sound like a struck slab, not a sung tone). In tone mode it is, in effect, a pulse-train-into-modal-bank with +-0.5 % period noise - distinctive (rough, 'kreischend') but close to a Membran/Schale body struck 440 times a second; the identity lives in the transitions. The tone will not 'lock' musically unless the modes are at f and the impulse rate is exactly f (they are, by construction), so intonation is fine but the timbre is harsh; Nachklang 0.6 s on 4 modes smears nothing at tone rate. Gestik tilt = Last is the best gesture (creak accelerating into a scream); Bebung in tone mode works via detune; in rhythm mode detune has no audible effect (rate 1-20 Hz +-50 ct = nothing) - Bebung must be mapped to body modes there.
soundBurst: Short gates (0.1-0.2 s) at default Last 0.45: rate = f/2^4.4 ~ 21/s at 440 Hz -> 2-4 slips per hit = a short ratchet ('Knarr-Kette') with a 0.4 s body ring-out - distinctive and tempo-robust; with vel = initial jerk the hit count varies, which keeps Puls lanes alive. Weakness: at y near 0 (rate 1.5-3/s) a 150-ms gate contains at most one slip or none -> a Puls lane can go silent on some steps; enforce >= 1 slip at gate start (initial jerk = guaranteed slip). At y > 0.75 a hit is a 150-ms buzz with the ring-out: usable, ordinary. Puls lanes have no Hoehe gesture, so the regime is set by the lane's Hoehe value - document it.
failureModes: Model constants not normalised to the period: at tone rates the block never re-sticks (hiss) or at creak rates the slip is sluggish (no click); the processor must scale stiffness/mass with the target rate.

Tone mode without a body is a buzz; with the body it is a struck modal slab excited at f - the 'scream' needs the click resonator (1.5-4 kHz) to track Last and vel, or it sounds like Membran at audio rate.
The 20-80 Hz crossover zone has no pitch identity and is unstable under Gestik Hoehe offsets (hysteresis needed in the worklet, plus a dead band ~0.1 wide).
y = 0 is near-silent (one creak every 0.7 s) - a floor of 1.5/s is specified but a lane hit shorter than the interval produces nothing; guarantee a slip at onset.
Bebung/detune has no audible effect in rhythm mode; map the detune bus to the body modes (they are at f anyway) so Gestik stays meaningful.
Native fallback cannot produce the rhythm regime; ship worklet-only and hide the engine without audioWorklet.
Polyphony: 3+ creaking fingers at different random rates is a woodshed, not music - works as texture only; L3 cross-coupling does not help with that.
verdict: Rare, not new: stick-slip creak models exist as academic and toolkit instruments (van den Doel's JASS creaking demo already maps normal force to creak rate, Thoret et al. DAFx 2013 go from creaky door to singing glass with one model, SC's Friction UGen and the Sound Design Toolkit ship it for Max/Pd, Croak is a Eurorack prototype) - but no touch instrument walks one finger axis from creak rhythm to a locked note, and that continuum is Kluft's real contribution. Worklet-only, ~0.5 units (L3 ~0.95); the native fallback cannot do the rhythm regime and should not ship. Held it is strongest in the creak-to-motorboat band (a rhythm the body pitches), weakest at the top, where it is a jittered impulse train through a modal bank - harsh, inharmonic, a struck slab at audio rate; Puls hits are a good short ratchet with variable slip count, provided a slip is guaranteed at onset. Build it, but normalise the physics to the period, put the hysteresis in the processor, route Bebung to the body in rhythm mode and sell it as a texture/lead hybrid with a narrow tone register.
